source.title: A Unifying Framework for Concept-Based Representational Similarity
source.authors: Gr'egoire Dhimoila; Victor Boutin; A. Picard; Thomas Fel; Thomas Serre

record.file_problem: The full paper is present and not cut off. Some appendix tables are flattened in the supplied text; the main vision table and Table 2 are assignable.
record.tranche_reason: The study audits concept-alignment objectives and reports that translation, concept consistency, and distributional matching do not reliably imply one another. It also shows conditions where alignment is low and where paired anchors plus combined objectives yield stronger alignment. It does not test convergence with model scale.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates concept-level alignment of SAEs trained on existing model embeddings, not whether raw representational distances between independently trained models become more alike as models scale. It reports human validation of its alignment benchmark, but that is not itself a result on the listed convergence versions. Results about model sizes, benchmark metrics, and zero-shot transfer are not evidence that alignment rises with model capability.
record.test_reason: The study learns SAE-mediated translation maps between frozen ViT, DINOv2 and SigLIP embeddings (and DINOv2 to RoBERTa). It reports how well one model's representations map onto another's, with full, scarce (1–0.1%) or no paired data. That bears on V4. Its key result is that pair-free objectives fail on real embeddings: distributional matching and cycle consistency do not recover instance-level translation. That is a specific challenge to V4's 'even without paired data' clause. Nothing in the study measures natural convergence across scale, cross-modal trends with capability, seed convergence, natural feature recurrence, or metric dependence. Concept consistency (same SAE index across models) is imposed by the training loss, not measured as arising on its own.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. Concept alignment splits into translation and concept consistency, each instance-wise or distributional, and these do not reliably imply one another. On real embeddings, purely unsupervised (distributional or cycle-consistency) objectives fail to recover instance-level alignment; in the synthetic DGP the instance/distributional duality does hold. CoSAE, which combines objectives with as little as 1% paired data, matches or exceeds crosscoders and USAEs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE-based concept extraction and InterVenchA translation/concept-consistency metrics, rather than the original sources’ geometric-similarity methods or scale sweeps. The paper tests alignment objectives, not the Platonic claim’s size/performance trend.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment scores change substantially with regularization choice and paired-data fraction. Instance-wise translation, concept consistency, distributional objectives, and mixed objectives produce different translation and concept-consistency outcomes; standalone versus aggregated crosscoder evaluation also changes the result.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept consistency (same SAE atom encoding the same concept across models) arises only when explicitly regularized. It is about 0 without coupling and up to 0.79–0.81 with paired anchors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model concept-index correspondence in SAEs is not identified by reconstruction or distributional matching and requires paired supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic generators, accurate within-view factor recovery does not align code indices across views (shared recall 0.025); instance translation does (0.975).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Identifiability of shared factors across separately trained dictionaries depends on instance-level coupling.

fits_no_version.finding: Crosscoder standalone encoder codes lose concept consistency (Mcont 0.000 vs 0.794 aggregated).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggregated-code alignment can mask non-aligned standalone encoders.

record.problems: The real-embedding evaluation uses proxy metrics rather than ground-truth concepts and covers a limited set of architectures and datasets. The authors note hyperparameter sensitivity and limitations in modeling domain-specific features. Some appendix table values are flattened in the supplied text. The study does not test scale or capability trends.
record.rows_left_out: The language InterVenchA table (Appendix K, Table A7) is not separately rowed because the supplied flattened layout does not support confident assignment of all reported values to regularization conditions and metrics. Other extraction-only metrics are omitted because they do not measure alignment. Human-validation results assess benchmark validity, not a listed convergence version.

untested.parts: All: no model-size or capability sweep.
All: cross-modal SAEs (CLIP towers, DINOv2–RoBERTa) are trained, but alignment is not related to model quality.
All: no comparison of networks across initialization seeds.
Linear or affine maps, model stitching and relative representations are not tested; only SAE-mediated encoder-to-decoder translation.
All: shared atom indices are imposed by training; natural recurrence of features or circuits is not measured.
All: no variation of similarity metric settings or input distribution for representational similarity.
All: natural cross-model alignment, plateau, and causes such as shared data are not measured.

Pair-free cycle-consistency SAE result: Mtr 0.072, Mcont 0.000
missing.locator: Section 4.2, On the Effect of Cycle Consistency

missing.what: Language cross-model translation (Gemma-2-9B vs Llama-3.1-8B): Mtr 0.66 with Ltr, 0.69–0.72 mixed, 0.18 distributional-only, 0.08 both-distributional
Multimodal CLIP image–text tower translation: Mtr 0.297 with Ltr, 0.505 mixed 1 in 1000, 0.000 distributional
Malign vs paired fraction p with and without distributional alignment, vision and text

record.verdict_notes: Many Table A9 values in the record are misassigned because the table is flattened. I reconstructed them by checking that each aggregate equals the mean of its components, and Table 2 confirms line (i): Mtr 0.732, Mcont 0.795. V-13/V-14 carry the wrong condition: row (g) is both-distributional. The record's V7 links are dropped: the study never measures natural cross-model alignment, and the zero concept consistency of uncoupled SAEs follows from arbitrary atom ordering, not from limited convergence. Synthetic, toy and method-comparison rows are unlinked. The study assumes a generative form of the PRH rather than testing it.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no measurement of raw distances between independently trained models as either changes.
The paper has a vision–text alignment experiment, but does not test whether vision and language representations become more aligned as both models improve.

It does not compare learned features or shared subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture. Its statement of little metric variance across SAE training seeds is not a test of shared features across seeds.
Tests SAE-based translation and concept consistency, plus cross-modal transfer. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data as a general mapping method.
Does not test recurrence of the same interpretable features or circuits across models.

Distinguishes translation from concept consistency and instance-wise from distributional objectives, but does not vary a similarity metric’s settings or input distribution to test metric/data dependence of representational convergence.

Shows incomplete or objective-dependent concept alignment in tested settings. Does not test whether natural alignment plateaus with scale, or establish that shared pretraining data or objectives explain convergence among pretrained models.

labels.condition: Vision cross-model (ViT/DINOv2/SigLIP) SAE translation with full or scarce (1 in 10, 1 in 100) paired data; DINOv2 to RoBERTa cross-modal transfer
labels.reason: V-03/V-11/V-15/V-17 establish useful trained translation, with corrected Mtr 0.7283/0.7331/0.7285/0.7317, but translation R² 0.4660/0.4705/0.5243/0.4224 qualifies V4's little-loss requirement. X-01 supports downstream transfer matching a dense projector, without measuring near-lossless representation recovery.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Same paired settings, judged on reconstruction loss; very scarce pairs; concept-only coupling
labels.reason: Table A9 reports incomplete translation reconstruction; V-19 drops to Mtr 0.6020 with 1 in 1000 pairs, and V-07 remains near the uncoupled baseline. V-07's exact corrected Mtr is 0.1400.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: No paired data (distributional or cycle-consistency objectives) on real vision embeddings
labels.reason: Corrected V-13 has Mtr 0.1428; corrected V-09 has 0.1402; V-05 has translation R² 0.0000. Section 4.2 reports cycle-consistency Mtr 0.072 and explicitly concludes that purely distributional objectives fail to recover instance-wise alignment. V-01 supplies an uncoupled control.

relation.reason: Its own experiments measure cross-model representation translation, supervision dependence, and downstream cross-modal transfer.

tranche.reason: The study directly tests translation between representations and shows that correspondence-free objectives fail to recover instance-wise alignment on real embeddings, qualifying V4.

source_check.notes: Mtr averages reconstruction, faithfulness, sparse probing, unlearning and TPP; it is not a fraction of representation information preserved. The table's extracted ordering is displaced, but component averages resolve the concept-only scores; Figure 6 supplies no recoverable numerical accuracy.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Jointly regularized vision CoSAE and CoSAE versus specialized methods
reader_labels.reason: Joint regularization yields high translation and concept-consistency metrics (V-11–V-12); CoSAE scores are competitive with or above the listed comparators (C-07–C-08), and the cross-modal mapping supports the reported zero-shot transfer (X-01).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Uncoupled, single-objective, and distributional-only alignment in the reported experiments
reader_labels.reason: The results show absent or partial scores for alignment properties not directly regularized, and low same-index shared-factor recall with reconstruction-only, consistency-only, and distributional objectives (A5-1–A5-10, V-01–V-10, T-01–T-02, T-04, T-06–T-07, T-09).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Strong alignment can be recovered with combined objectives and mixed training; the paper reports high shared-factor recall under instance translation or the full objective, showing that alignment is not uniformly far from complete in these tested settings (V-11–V-20, T-03, T-05, T-08, T-10).
